title: PICK: An SRAM-based Processing-in-Memory Accelerator for K-Nearest-Neighbor Search in Point Clouds
problem: K-nearest neighbor (kNN) search on point clouds is computationally intense and memory-heavy, but off-chip memory access dominates latency and energy. Current approaches struggle with resource-constrained scenarios typical in edge AI and autonomous driving.
motivation: Point cloud processing is critical for autonomous driving and 3D perception; accelerating kNN with minimal memory access enables real-time, energy-efficient inference on edge devices.
method: PICK is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture using bit-serial PIM (BS-PIM) to perform kNN search with on-chip SRAM, eliminating off-chip access. Includes: (1) bit-width clipping for bit-serial distance calculation with reduced latency; (2) filtering-and-selection strategy achieving approximately constant time for arbitrary k; (3) two-stage pipeline parallelizing distance calculation and top-k selection.
key_novelty: Bit-serial PIM architecture with filtering-and-selection strategy and two-stage pipelining to achieve constant-time kNN selection within on-chip SRAM, eliminating off-chip memory bottleneck.
contributions: Bit-width clipping for reduced latency with minimal accuracy loss
Filtering-and-selection strategy for approximate constant-time k-selection
Two-stage pipeline for latency hiding and throughput improvement
limitations: Evaluation on specific point cloud datasets; scalability to extremely large point clouds and batch kNN queries not discussed.
primary_theme: Bit-serial PIM architecture for accelerated kNN search in point clouds
